tool_calls.output:
### Streaming support and memory
- **Chinese targets:** This page does **not establish Chinese output availability**, either written or spoken, for SeamlessStreaming or the unified Seamless model. It describes streaming speech input with text/audio output, but gives no target-language breakdown.
- **Chinese mention elsewhere:** The expressive-model evaluation example marks `cmn` as experimental; that does not establish streaming support.
- **Memory:** No RAM or VRAM minimums appear. The streaming model’s listed size is **2.5 billion parameters**, not a memory requirement. Precompiled fairseq2 packages are described as available for Linux x86-64 and Apple-silicon Macs.

### Licensing by component
| Component | License listed |
|---|---|
| Repository code | [MIT](MIT_LICENSE) |
| W2v-BERT 2.0 encoder | [MIT](MIT_LICENSE) |
| SeamlessM4T, both generations | [CC-BY-NC 4.0](LICENSE) |
| SeamlessStreaming | [CC-BY-NC 4.0](LICENSE) |
| Unified Seamless and SeamlessExpressive | [Seamless-specific terms](SEAMLESS_LICENSE) |

Expressive-model access requires approval through a [download request](https://ai.meta.com/resources/models-and-libraries/seamless-downloads/); the page also points to an [acceptable-use policy](ACCEPTABLE_USE_POLICY).

### Dated announcements
- **2023-12-18:** W2v-BERT 2.0 encoder publication.
- **2023-12-14:** NeurIPS tutorial publication.
- No explicit model-release dates appear for the streaming, expressive, unified, or M4T v2 models.

### Relevant references
- **Streaming:** [Model card](https://huggingface.co/facebook/seamless-streaming), [model documentation](docs/streaming/README.md), [evaluation/inference instructions](src/seamless_communication/cli/streaming).
- **Expressive:** [Model card](https://huggingface.co/facebook/seamless-expressive), [documentation](docs/expressive/README.md).
- **Unified model:** Uses the streaming model with an expressive vocoder substituted; see [inference documentation](src/seamless_communication/inference).
- **M4T v2:** [Model card](https://huggingface.co/facebook/seamless-m4t-v2-large), [documentation](docs/m4t/README.md).
- **Speech encoder:** [Model card](https://huggingface.co/facebook/conformer-shaw).

tool_calls.input: {"url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ictnlp/StreamSpeech/main/README.md", "prompt": "Extract target languages available EN to Chinese? true streaming mechanics, checkpoints, code/weight licenses, hardware memory and dates."}
tool_calls.output:
- **Translation directions:** Available checkpoints cover French → English, Spanish → English, and German → English. **English → Chinese is not listed**; English is the only listed target language.
- **Streaming mechanics:** Audio is processed in adjustable chunks using `--source-segment-size` (milliseconds); the example uses 320 ms. The model incrementally provides source transcriptions, translated text, and synthesized speech. Intermediate text can be enabled with `--output-asr-translation`. Word-by-word speech synthesis is supported; the cascade variant’s TTS component can operate independently on incremental text. Chunk duration is **not** an end-to-end latency guarantee.
- **Checkpoints:** Each listed direction has UnitY, offline StreamSpeech, and simultaneous StreamSpeech weights, downloadable through Hugging Face or Baidu. Speech generation additionally uses an English unit-based HiFi-GAN vocoder, with checkpoint and configuration links provided.
- **Code/weight licenses:** Neither license is specified in the supplied content. Public download links alone do not establish reuse permissions.
- **Hardware / memory:** Examples select one GPU through CUDA. No GPU model, minimum VRAM, system RAM, or checkpoint size is given. Dependencies specify Python 3.10, PyTorch 2.0.1, fairseq, and SimulEval.
- **Dates:** June 5, 2024: paper, repository, weights, and demo announced. June 17, 2024: local-browser GUI announced. June 17, 2025: related Stream-Omni project announced. StreamSpeech is identified as an ACL 2024 paper.

- **Language direction:** French → English only; Chinese is not supported.
- **Streaming:** Translates while the speaker is talking, emitting translated audio and timestamped text incrementally. Output runs at 12.5 Hz; context spans 40 seconds, with training sequences reaching 120 seconds.
- **Hardware/backends:** PyTorch; MLX on Macs; Rust with NVIDIA CUDA or Mac Metal. The smaller model targets on-device use. Experimental MLX-Swift support was tested on iPhone 16 Pro.
- **Licensing:** Python and browser-client code: MIT. Rust backend: Apache, with no version specified. Model weights: CC-BY 4.0.
- **Dates:** The cited paper is dated 2025. No explicit release or update date appears in the supplied content.

## Model Introduction Hy-MT2 is a family of “fast-thinking” multilingual translation models designed for complex real-world scenarios. It includes three model sizes: 1.8B, 7B, and 30B-A3B (MoE), all of which support translation among 33 languages and effectively follow translation instructions in multiple languages. For on-device deployment, AngelSlim 1.25-bit extreme quantization reduces the storage requirement of the 1.8B model to only 440 MB and improves inference speed by 1.5x. Multi-dimensional evaluations show that Hy-MT2 delivers outstanding performance across general, real-world business, domain-specific, and instruction-following translation tasks. The 7B and 30B-A3B models outperform open-source models such as DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Kimi K2.6 in fast-thinking mode, while the lightweight 1.8B model also surpasses mainstream commercial APIs from providers such as Microsoft and Doubao overall. In this release, we also open-source [IFMTBench](./IFMTBench/README.md), a benchmark for evaluating translation instruction-following capabilities. We also welcome everyone to use our released Hy-MT2-Translator Skill, which makes it easy to integrate Hy-MT2 series models for translation tasks. Download links: [ClawHub](https://clawhub.ai/tencent-adm/hy-mt2-translator-skill) and [SkillHub](https://skillhub.cn/skills/hy-mt2-translator). Now, Tencent Hy is officially partnering with WMT26 for the "Video Subtitle Translation Task" (https://www2.statmt.org/wmt26/video-subtitle-translation.html). Participants who use the Hy-MT model series to compete in the "General Machine Translation Task" (https://www2.statmt.org/wmt26/translation-task.html) and the "Video Subtitle Translation Task" will have the chance to win special awards sponsored by Hunyuan.
